paragraphs.source_en: At Nijō Castle, Tokugawa Ieyasu took off the battle surcoat that had scarcely left his back for so long and welcomed the New Year of Keichō 20. One of his wishes had been fulfilled, and at last he could breathe more easily, yet his heart remained clouded one moment and clear the next.

units.source_en: At Nijō Castle, Tokugawa Ieyasu took off the battle surcoat that had scarcely left his back for so long and welcomed the New Year of Keichō 20.

paragraphs.source_en: The outcome had largely accorded with Ieyasu's wishes: peace had been concluded, and he had laid aside his battle surcoat. But could the daimyō throughout the realm, and the rōnin gathered around Hideyori, truly understand how hard-won this peace had been? The matter was by no means completely settled. Whenever he thought of this, he could not set his mind at ease.

units.source_en: The outcome had largely accorded with Ieyasu's wishes: peace had been concluded, and he had laid aside his battle surcoat.
units.source_zh: 结果大致遂了家康的心愿，和议缔结，阵羽织也脱下来了。

units.source_en: But could the daimyō throughout the realm, and the rōnin gathered around Hideyori, truly understand how hard-won this peace had been?

paragraphs.source_zh: 结果大致遂了家康的心愿，和议缔结，阵羽织也脱下来了。但是，天下大名，还有那些聚在秀赖身边的浪人，果真能明白太平的来之不易吗？事情绝未完全解决。一想到这些，他就放心不下。

paragraphs.source_en: In the eyes of some, Ieyasu had become an incorrigible old man who could not bear to be left in peace. He held the realm in his hands—why must he make trouble for a mere boy?

units.source_en: In the eyes of some, Ieyasu had become an incorrigible old man who could not bear to be left in peace.

units.source_en: He held the realm in his hands—why must he make trouble for a mere boy?
units.source_zh: 他指点江山，却为何要和一介小儿过不去？

paragraphs.source_zh: 在一些世人眼中，家康已变成一个让人无可奈何的耐不住寂寞的老人。他指点江山，却为何要和一介小儿过不去？

paragraphs.source_en: Can it be that no one in this age understands my intentions? Ieyasu, often ill at this time, felt an inexpressible loneliness, anxiety, and anguish welling within him.

units.source_en: Can it be that no one in this age understands my intentions?
units.source_zh: 莫非当世竟无人能领会我的心意？

units.source_en: Ieyasu, often ill at this time, felt an inexpressible loneliness, anxiety, and anguish welling within him.
units.source_zh: 此际多有病恙的家康，心中生出难以言表的寂寞、焦虑与痛苦。

paragraphs.source_zh: 莫非当世竟无人能领会我的心意？此际多有病恙的家康，心中生出难以言表的寂寞、焦虑与痛苦。

paragraphs.source_en: Neither Hidetada nor Hideyori understands my true heart—though the crushing burden of this anxiety was almost more than he could bear, Ieyasu had not yet despaired. Yet, as Date Masamune and Tōdō Takatora had said, if the peace won through such painful effort brought only a brief truce, it was no laughing matter. Ieyasu reflected that this might be the final trial the gods and buddhas had set him in this life.

units.source_en: Ieyasu reflected that this might be the final trial the gods and buddhas had set him in this life.
units.source_zh: 家康思量，这恐是神佛对他今生最后的考验。

paragraphs.source_zh: 无论秀忠还是秀赖，都无法知我真心——尽管这种焦虑的重荷压得人不堪其沉，但家康仍未绝望。可是，正如伊达政宗和藤堂高虎所说，若费尽苦心缔结的太平，只是带来片刻的休战，就不能一笑置之了。家康思量，这恐是神佛对他今生最后的考验。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had already sent Hidetada a message: “Kyoto is bitterly cold in winter. Go home promptly after the New Year.”

units.source_en: Ieyasu had already sent Hidetada a message: “Kyoto is bitterly cold in winter. Go home promptly after the New Year.”
units.source_zh: 对于秀忠，家康早就送上了一句话：“京都冬天太冷，过年后早早回去吧。”

paragraphs.source_zh: 对于秀忠，家康早就送上了一句话：“京都冬天太冷，过年后早早回去吧。”

paragraphs.source_en: That no one in the realm knew Ieyasu's heart was both his own sorrow and the sorrow of the realm. Enough, enough. Better to leave this whirlpool for a while and quietly watch how events unfolded.

units.source_en: That no one in the realm knew Ieyasu's heart was both his own sorrow and the sorrow of the realm.

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康之心，天下皆不知，既是他自身之痛，也是天下之痛。罢了罢了，莫如暂时离开这旋涡，静观事态变化。

paragraphs.source_en: An individual's wisdom is always limited; a truly wise person must know how to heed others and adopt whatever is good in their counsel. Thus, the wisdom of the truly wise never ceases to grow. Deep in contemplation, Ieyasu entered his seventy-fourth year.

units.source_en: An individual's wisdom is always limited; a truly wise person must know how to heed others and adopt whatever is good in their counsel.
units.source_zh: 个人的智慧总会有限，所谓真正的智者，必定善于倾听别人的意思，择其善为己所用。

units.source_en: Thus, the wisdom of the truly wise never ceases to grow.
units.source_zh: 因此，真正智者的智慧，永远不会停滞。

units.source_en: Deep in contemplation, Ieyasu entered his seventy-fourth year.
units.source_zh: 家康在思索中迎来了七十有四高寿。

paragraphs.source_zh: 个人的智慧总会有限，所谓真正的智者，必定善于倾听别人的意思，择其善为己所用。因此，真正智者的智慧，永远不会停滞。家康在思索中迎来了七十有四高寿。

paragraphs.source_en: The plans for a year begin in spring. Ieyasu respected custom and family tradition more than most. Yet empty ceremony, cumbersome formalities, extravagance, and waste were contrary to his nature.

units.source_en: The plans for a year begin in spring.
units.source_zh: 一年之计在于春。

units.source_en: Ieyasu respected custom and family tradition more than most.
units.source_zh: 家康比常人更尊重习俗和家风。

units.source_en: Yet empty ceremony, cumbersome formalities, extravagance, and waste were contrary to his nature.
units.source_zh: 不过，拘于虚礼的繁文缛节与奢糜浪费，却与他的性情不符。

paragraphs.source_zh: 一年之计在于春。家康比常人更尊重习俗和家风。不过，拘于虚礼的繁文缛节与奢糜浪费，却与他的性情不符。

paragraphs.source_en: Though he detested needless waste, once he had accepted the origin of a custom and established it as a house rule, Ieyasu would permit no alteration. On New Year's Eve, he personally inspected the cranes to be presented to the Imperial Court, then retired amid the bells of all the temples ringing together to dispel the hundred and eight worldly passions.

units.source_en: Though he detested needless waste, once he had accepted the origin of a custom and established it as a house rule, Ieyasu would permit no alteration.
units.source_zh: 尽管憎恶无谓的浪费，但一旦认定其来历，并将其定为家规，家康就绝不再允许变更。

units.source_en: On New Year's Eve, he personally inspected the cranes to be presented to the Imperial Court, then retired amid the bells of all the temples ringing together to dispel the hundred and eight worldly passions.
units.source_zh: 除夕之日，他亲自检视了进献给宫中的鹤，然后在诸寺一齐撞响的除去百八烦恼的钟声之中就寝。

paragraphs.source_zh: 尽管憎恶无谓的浪费，但一旦认定其来历，并将其定为家规，家康就绝不再允许变更。除夕之日，他亲自检视了进献给宫中的鹤，然后在诸寺一齐撞响的除去百八烦恼的钟声之中就寝。

paragraphs.source_en: Chōfukumaru, too, had probably noticed that his father presented cranes to the Court while their own household ate only rabbit, and the contrast had raised a question in his mind. After completing his devotions and entering the Buddha hall, Chōfukumaru said, “Our forefathers, father and son, must have suffered greatly as they wandered from place to place.”

units.source_en: After completing his devotions and entering the Buddha hall, Chōfukumaru said, “Our forefathers, father and son, must have suffered greatly as they wandered from place to place.”

paragraphs.source_en: Whatever he was thinking, Chōfukumaru gave a long, emphatic “Hmm.” It had been father and son then, and it was father and son now; the thought must have stirred in him the particular sentiment of youth.

units.source_zh: 当年是父子俩，现在也是父子俩，他必是对此产生了少年特有的感怀。

paragraphs.source_en: Since the warrior houses customarily offered their New Year greetings at the Imperial Court on the third day of the first month, Ieyasu merely presented cranes to the Court on the first and decided to send Ōsawa Motoyado to offer formal greetings on the third.

units.source_en: Since the warrior houses customarily offered their New Year greetings at the Imperial Court on the third day of the first month, Ieyasu merely presented cranes to the Court on the first and decided to send Ōsawa Motoyado to offer formal greetings on the third.
units.source_zh: 由于武家向宫中朝贺的日子，例为正月初三，故初一，家康只向宫中献了鹤，决定初三再次令大泽基宿进宫朝贺。

paragraphs.source_en: On New Year's Day, from the moment he began the customary festive meal, daimyō and monks arrived without pause, filling the great hall as each visitor's name was announced.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had believed that he would never again greet a New Year in this world. Yet before he had even left Kyoto, Hideyori, the person who troubled him most, had sent an envoy who reached Nijō Castle early on New Year's morning. Hideyori must have had this on his mind since the previous night and dispatched the envoy at the earliest hour.

paragraphs.source_en: To see neither life nor death is the state of an enlightened master; yet once dead, one can no longer keep company with the living—such is the reality of ordinary mortals. Before I vanish, while my figure can still appear before the eyes of the world, is there some important task I have forgotten to perform?
